created_at_note: hashed into ledger event 0 BEFORE any run of this study
question: Does archive-based parent selection (skill-memory consumption) accelerate coverage/QD growth in a NEW environment vs fresh sampling, and does local accumulation matter beyond pure consumption?

environment.maze: B1 (vertical chambers) regenerated from GEN-v2 generator, seed 201
environment.walls_sha256_note: first 16 hex shown here are prefix of full digest recorded in ledger; full digest equals ledger event 0 of GEN-v2
environment.prechecks: package SHA256SUMS 89/89, GEN-v1 ledger 94 events VALID, GEN-v2 ledger 76 events VALID, B1 hashes match GEN-v2 ledger event 0 (fail-closed)

config.variation_mode: mutation-only (package's best-known operator policy per rejected H2), identical rng call order in all arms: two integers draws + one choice draw + gaussian_mutation(p1, sigma_mut*1.5, 0.5)

T_transfer_seed.gen0: 256 elites sampled UNIFORMLY WITHOUT replacement (rng=default_rng(seed).choice) from frozen source archive full_seed{seed}, evaluated on B1, inserted into local archive as immigrants with their source ids recorded as parents
T_transfer_seed.gen1_plus: variation parents drawn from local (growing) archive
T_transfer_seed.pairing: T run with seed s consumes full_seed{s}

R_random_seed.gen0: 256 random genomes N(0,1.2) clip +/-4, rng=default_rng(seed).normal — identical to package initial populations
R_random_seed.gen1_plus: variation parents drawn from local (growing) archive

F_frozen_parents.gen0: identical to R (same rng call: normal(0,1.2,(256,74)))
F_frozen_parents.gen1_plus: variation parents ALWAYS drawn from frozen source archive full_seed{seed}; local archive accumulates children for measurement only (consumption without accumulation)

budget_fairness: all arms: 256 gen-0 evals + 96/generation x 151 batches = 14,656 evaluations on B1, same seeds, same code path for evaluation and archive admission

per_generation: qd_score = sum of elite fitness on B1
migrant_parent_count (arm T: parents[:,0] < 256, i.e. gen-0 immigrant ids)

hypothesis.claim: Archive parent selection accelerates diversity/quality growth in a new environment relative to fresh random initialization.
hypothesis.test_plan: 3 arms x 3 seeds on maze B1; means over seeds at checkpoints 50 and 150; all seeds reported, none dropped.
hypothesis.verdict_rule: SUPPORTED_IN_THIS_LAB if mean_T_qd(50) >= 1.10*mean_R_qd(50) AND mean_T_qd(150) >= 1.10*mean_R_qd(150) AND mean_T_cov(50) - mean_R_cov(50) >= 0.05; REJECTED_BY_THRESHOLD if any of the three fails; UNKNOWN on execution failure.
hypothesis.kill_condition: If mean_T_qd <= mean_R_qd at BOTH checkpoints, record label 'archive_consumption_worthless' as a negative finding. No threshold may change after observing results.
hypothesis.descriptive: Arm F curves and final values; migrant-parent share trajectory in arm T; gen-0 baseline state (recorded, not part of verdict).

ledger_plan: new receipts_gen3.jsonl ('x' mode, no resume); event 0 = this file's sha256 + arm specs + B1 hashes; one event per generation per run with unique selected_parent_ids (consumption evidence) and candidate weights hash; integrity_gen3.json with head/count
stop_conditions: NaN/Inf in evaluation or hash mismatch in prechecks => STOP/BLOCKED, no interpretation
inference_limits: one held-out maze (B1) of one structural family; one operator policy (mutation-only); 3 seeds; no p-values
acceleration claim bounded to coverage/QD under this metric; no mission-level value claim
T advantage at gen 0 is partly structural (diverse immigrants start ahead); verdict checkpoints 50/150 test persistence, and this caveat is recorded, not hidden
local simulation; propose-only; no Core/hardware/money; production_authorized=false
